evidence_basis.evidence_gap_note: Mapped P2 evidence supports the assessment patterns. No P1 lesson assignment inferred.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes two coherent waves?

options.B: They always have zero phase difference
options.C: They have a constant phase difference
options.D: They always travel in opposite directions

questions.prompt: Two equal waves overlap in antiphase at a point. What is the resultant amplitude there?
Two in-phase sources produce waves of wavelength λ. Which path difference gives destructive interference for equal amplitudes?

figure.purpose: Assess path-difference classification from a spatial layout.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white line diagram with in-phase sources S1 and S2 and point P. Label S1P = 26 cm and S2P = 35 cm. State wavelength 6.0 cm beside the diagram. Do not show wavefront counts or the answer.
figure.alt_text: Two in-phase sources have routes of 26 cm and 35 cm to point P.

parts.prompt: Calculate the path difference at P.
Express the path difference as a multiple of the wavelength.
State and explain the type of interference at P.
Two coherent waves arrive in phase at a point. Their amplitudes are 3.5 mm and 2.0 mm. Calculate the resultant amplitude.
The phase of one wave is changed by 180°. Calculate the new resultant amplitude and explain why cancellation is incomplete.

figure.purpose: Mix earlier signed-superposition reasoning with current phase and coherence analysis.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white three-column table for times t1, t2 and t3. At point Q, wave X has displacements +2.0 mm, 0, -2.0 mm and wave Y has +1.0 mm, 0, -1.0 mm. Below it, show a separate pair of phase markers whose separation changes between t1 and t3. No result row.
figure.alt_text: A table lists signed displacements of two waves and separate phase markers that drift with time.

parts.prompt: Use the principle of superposition to determine the resultant displacement at Q at t1, t2 and t3.
For the separate phase-marker pair, state whether the waves are coherent and explain your answer.
Explain why superposition can still be applied at an instant even when two waves are not coherent.
